headline: U.S. Judge Temporarily Halts East Potomac Park Closure
deck: The order protects regular public access through Nov. 28, but does not require the government to manage the park.
body: Judge Ana Reyes of the U.S. District Court ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course near the White House, blocking for now President Donald Trump’s plan to redevelop the site along the Potomac River into a championship-level venue. [E1] [E2]
She issued the temporary restraining order before East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months. [E2]
Her order enjoins the government from closing East Potomac Park and its golf course during the daily hours in which they were open on Nov. 14. [E3]
The order is in effect through Nov. 28 or until a further court order, whichever comes first. [E4]

CNN reported that Reyes said the administration’s push to revamp East Potomac Golf Links into the championship course Trump desires was one of several construction projects he has sought as part of an effort to remake Washington to his tastes and leave a legacy. She said the plan likely violated environmental law and procedural safeguards for executive-branch actions. [E5]
The ruling does not require the Trump administration to actively manage the park or golf course, CBS News reported. [E6]
The park shall remain open and accessible to the public, subject to routine temporary closures needed for imminent public-safety threats, according to The Hill’s account of the order. [E7]
